The '''2013–14 [[Cypriot First Division]]''' was the 75th season of the Cypriot top-level [[Association football|football]] league. It began on 31 August 2013 and ended on 31 May 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/14708|script-title=el:Το ημερολογιακό πρόγραμμα της νέας χρονιάς|language=el|publisher=CFA|date=3 June 2013|access-date=10 June 2013}}</ref> [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] were the defending champions.

The league comprised eleven teams from the [[2012–13 Cypriot First Division|2012–13 season]] and three promoted teams from the [[2012–13 Cypriot Second Division|2012–13 Second Division]].

The 17 May 2014 title deciding match between [[AEL Limassol]] and [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] was abandoned (at 0–0) after 52 minutes, when a bomb thrown by AEL fans, hit and injured APOEL's player [[Kaká (footballer born 1981)|Kaká]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sg.news.yahoo.com/cyprus-title-decider-abandoned-firework-injures-player-181841285--sow.html|title=Cyprus title decider abandoned after firework injures player|website=sg.news.yahoo.com}}</ref> The match was replayed behind closed doors at a neutral stadium on 31 May 2014 and APOEL achieved to win their second consecutive league title after beating AEL Limassol by 1–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=cyp/news/newsid=2102109.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140605050918/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=cyp/news/newsid=2102109.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 June 2014|title=Sheridan strike hands APOEL Cypriot title|publisher=UEFA|date=31 May 2014|access-date=31 May 2014}}</ref> However, on 6 June 2014, the [[Cyprus Football Association]]’s (CFA) disciplinary committee – acting as an appeals board – unanimously cancelled on the CFA council’s decision to repeat the 17 May championship final, awarding the match to APOEL with a 0–3 score.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cyprus-mail.com/2014/06/07/26013/|title=APOEL are champions… again!|publisher=cyprus-mail.com|date=6 June 2014|access-date=6 June 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714142458/http://cyprus-mail.com/2014/06/07/26013/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Teams==

===Promotion and relegation (pre-season)===
[[AEP Paphos F.C.|AEP Paphos]] and [[Ayia Napa F.C.|Ayia Napa]] were relegated at the end of the first stage of the [[2012–13 Cypriot First Division|2012–13 season]] after finishing in the bottom two places of the table. They were joined by [[Olympiakos Nicosia]], who finished at the bottom of the second-phase Group C.

The relegated teams were replaced by [[2012–13 Cypriot Second Division|2012–13 Second Division]] champions [[Aris Limassol F.C.|Aris Limassol]], runners-up [[AEK Kouklia F.C.|AEK Kouklia]] and third-placed team [[Ermis Aradippou]].

|note_ENP=On 17 May 2013, [[Enosis Neon Paralimni FC|Enosis Neon Paralimni]] were deducted three points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed to meet the financial criteria of [[UEFA]].<ref name="cfa.com.cy"/>
|note_ALK=On 17 May 2013, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted three points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed to meet the financial criteria of [[UEFA]].<ref name="cfa.com.cy"/>
On 6 August 2013, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted another three points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed again to meet the financial criteria of [[UEFA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/15210|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Πρωτοβάθμιας Επιτροπής Κριτηρίων|language=el |publisher=CFA |date=6 August 2013|access-date=6 August 2013}}</ref>
On 8 November 2013, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted six points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed for the third time to meet the financial criteria of [[UEFA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/16269|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Πρωτοβάθμιας Επιτροπής Κριτηρίων|language=el |publisher=CFA |date=8 November 2013|access-date=8 November 2013}}</ref>
On 2 December 2013, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted two points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed to meet [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]]'s monthly financial criteria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/16562|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Πρωτοβάθμιας Επιτροπής Κριτηρίων για μηνιαίο έλεγχο Σωματείων|language=el |publisher=CFA |date=2 December 2013|access-date=2 December 2013}}</ref>
On 8 January 2014, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted nine points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed to pay the referees' salaries in three of their home matches (deducted three points for each match).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/16962|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Δικαστικής Επιτροπής|language=el |publisher=CFA |date=8 January 2014|access-date=8 January 2014}}</ref>
On 15 January 2014, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted three points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed again to pay the referees' salaries in two of their home matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/17070|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Δικαστικής Επιτροπής|language=el |publisher=CFA |date=15 January 2014|access-date=15 January 2014}}</ref>
On 31 January 2014, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted two points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed for the fourth time to meet the financial criteria of [[UEFA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/17300|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Πρωτοβάθμιας Επιτροπής Κριτηρίων |language=el |publisher=CFA |date=31 January 2014|access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref>
On 5 February 2014, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted nine points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed again to pay the referees' salaries in three of their home matches (deducted three points for each match).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/17361|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Δικαστικής Επιτροπής|language=el |publisher=CFA |date=5 February 2014|access-date=5 February 2014}}</ref>
On 6 March 2014, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted two points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed for the fifth time to meet the financial criteria of [[UEFA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/17746|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Πρωτοβάθμιας Επιτροπής Κριτηρίων |language=el |publisher=CFA |date=6 March 2014|access-date=6 March 2014}}</ref>
On 9 April 2014, [[Alki Larnaca F.C.|Alki Larnaca]] were deducted two points by [[Cyprus Football Association|CFA]] because they failed for the sixth time to meet the financial criteria of [[UEFA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/18181/17|script-title=el:Αποφάσεις Πρωτοβάθμιας Επιτροπής Κριτηρίων|language=el|publisher=CFA|date=9 April 2014|access-date=9 April 2014|title = Ειδήσεις - Αποφάσεις Πρωτοβάθμιας Επιτροπής Κριτηρίων  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923222026/http://www.cfa.com.cy/Gr/news/18181/17|archive-date=23 September 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

*Fastest goal of the season: '''18 seconds''' – {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Césinha]] ([[Ermis Aradippou|Ermis]]) against [[Nea Salamis Famagusta FC|Nea Salamina]] (''24 November 2013'')
*Latest goal of the season: '''97 minutes and 4 seconds''' – {{flagicon|ISR}} [[Roberto Colautti]] ([[Anorthosis Famagusta FC|Anorthosis]]) against [[AC Omonia|Omonia]] (''31 August 2013'')
*First scored penalty kick of the season: '''48 minutes and 2 seconds''' – {{flagicon|ARG}} [[Pablo Vranjicán]] ([[AEK Kouklia F.C.|AEK Kouklia]]) against [[AEK Larnaca F.C.|AEK Larnaca]] (''21:03 [[Eastern European Time|EET]], 31 August 2013'')
*First own goal of the season: '''56 minutes and 21 seconds''' – {{flagicon|BRA}} [[Diego Gaúcho]] ([[AEL Limassol|AEL]]) for [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] (''20:24 [[Eastern European Time|EET]], 14 September 2013'')

**{{flagicon|BRA}} [[Marcos De Azevedo]] ([[Ermis Aradippou|Ermis]]) against [[Doxa Katokopias F.C.|Doxa]] (''21 September 2013'')

* First red card of the season: '''68 minutes''' – {{flagicon|LIT}} [[Ernestas Šetkus]] for [[Nea Salamis Famagusta FC|Nea Salamina]] against [[Doxa Katokopias F.C.|Doxa]] (''19:23 [[Eastern European Time|EET]], 1 September 2013'')

** [[Doxa Katokopias F.C.|Doxa]] 1–1 [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] – 1 for Doxa ([[Richard Kingson]]) and 1 for APOEL ([[Aritz Borda]]) (''23 November 2013'')
